case_name: Kuria and another v State of Rajasthan
respondent:
State of Rajasthan
Supreme Court of India

13 September 2012
Cr.A. No. 2488 of 2009
The Judgment was delivered by : Swatanter Kumar, J.
1.  At the outset, we may notice that 15 accused persons had faced trial for offences u/ss. 302 and 364 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "IPC") before the Court of the Additional Sessions Judge, Banswara (Rajasthan). Vide its judgment dated 5th September, 2003, learned Trial Court acquitted all the accused persons except Laleng son of Bajeng, Laleng son of Dalji and Kuriya son of Laleng. These three accused were convicted for both these offences and were directed to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life with a fine of Rs.4,000/ each and in default to further undergo rigorous imprisonment for four months under Section 302/34 IPC and to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten years with a fine of Rs.1000/each and in default to undergo further rigorous imprisonment for one month under Section 364/34 IPC.
2.  All
facts: The case involves 15 accused persons who faced trial for offences under sections 302 and 364 of the Indian Penal Code.
The Trial Court acquitted all the accused except three, who were convicted and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for life with a fine.
The High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence.
The appellants argue that the prosecution's case is based on suspicion and that there are serious holes in the case.
The post-mortem report shows 15 injuries caused by blunt objects within 24 hours of death.
issues: Whether the prosecution has established its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Whether the accused have been properly convicted and sentenced.
Whether the High Court's confirmation of the conviction is justified.
petitioner_arguments: PW1 is not a reliable eye-witness, inasmuch as from his statement and the attendant circumstances, it is clear that he has not seen the occurrence.
Presence of PW15 at the place of occurrence is doubtful inasmuch as PW3 in his report to the Police did not name him.
No specific role or use of a particular weapon in causing injuries by the respective accused has been seen by PW3 or any other witness.

There is clear contradiction between the ocular and medical evidence inasmuch as, according to PW3 and PW15, axe and kash were used for inflicting injuries upon the deceased, while, according to the post mortem report, all the injuries were caused with blunt weapons and there was no bleeding injury.
The statement of hostile witnesses or unreliable witnesses cannot be used for the purposes of corroboration of other witnesses.
court_reasoning: The court notes that the prosecution's case is based on suspicion and that there are serious holes in the case.
The court refers to the post-mortem report, which shows 15 injuries caused by blunt objects within 24 hours of death.
The court concludes that the prosecution has not established its case beyond reasonable doubt.
holding: The appeal is allowed, and the conviction and sentence are set aside.
